citation.description: Provenance for a single figure. Required whenever a value is present.

as_of.description: Date the figure was reported, not the date scraped.

quote.description: Short supporting excerpt. Keep under 300 chars.

metric.description: A single quantitative figure with full provenance. `basis` must state exactly what the number counts — this is what keeps estimates from laundering into facts.

is_estimate.description: TRUE unless the figure is a company-reported line item. Segment revenue that a company reports (e.g. NVDA Data Center) is NOT an estimate; anything analyst-derived IS.

basis.description: What the number actually counts and how it was derived. e.g. 'Reported Data Center segment revenue, Q2 FY2026, x4'.

id.description: Stable slug. Never reuse or renumber — links reference this.

segment.description: Primary segment id from taxonomy.json. Drives container membership.

also_operates.description: Secondary segment ids. Microsoft is hyperscale AND enterprise_ai AND gpu_cloud. Renders as a visual cue, does not move the node.

verticals.description: Vertical ids from taxonomy.json. Drives the sidebar 'Isolate Healthcare AI' filter.

period.description: Exactly what window every metric on this node covers. e.g. 'Q2 FY2026 annualized (run-rate)'.

revenue_ai.description: AI-attributable revenue. Almost always an estimate — very few companies report an AI line item.

operating_margin_pct.description: May be negative. Color scale for this metric MUST be diverging around zero.

summary.description: Qualitative analysis shown in the intelligence panel. Write for a reader who already knows the company.

bottleneck.description: Hudson Labs tracks 14 bottlenecks; this is the chokepoint thesis made explicit.

criticality.description: 5 = no viable substitute at scale today (ASML EUV, TSMC N3/N2).

revenue_growth_yoy_pct.description: YoY growth on the AI-attributable line where available, else total. Arguably matters more than absolute revenue in this sector.

analyst.description: Populates the right-hand intelligence panel. Written as a research note, not a company description. This is the progressive-disclosure payload.

p_and_l_drivers.description: What actually moves the P&L. e.g. 'HBM attach rate', 'utilization on contracted GPU fleet'.

key_debate.description: The one thing bulls and bears actually disagree about. Not a summary.

read_across.description: Names that move on this company's print, and why.

customer_concentration.description: From the 10-K concentration disclosure where available. The risk that one counterparty's capex decision is the whole thesis.

valuation.description: Point-in-time market data. Goes stale within a DAY, unlike fundamentals which are quarterly. Refreshed on its own cadence by the pipeline; always render with as_of visible.

ev_revenue.description: EV / NTM revenue. The primary comp-set metric for this sector.

last_round_valuation_usd_m.description: Private companies only. Note the date — a 2024 mark is not a 2026 mark.

ev_gross_profit.description: Better than EV/S for comparing businesses with very different gross margins — which is exactly this stack.

notes.description: Caveats on how the share count was derived — multi-class resolution, ADR skips. Surfaces silently-wrong market caps instead of burying them.

venture.description: Private-company economics. Public filings have no analogue for most of this, and none of it is audited — every field here is an estimate unless the company disclosed it directly.

funding_tier.description: Drives the private node's visual framing.

post_money_usd_m.description: Implied post-money at the last priced round. A 2024 mark is NOT a 2026 mark — always read with last_round_date.

estimated_arr_usd_m.description: ARR, which for AI-native companies is usually an annualized run-rate rather than contracted recurring revenue. Not the same quality of number as GAAP revenue.

nrr_pct.description: Net revenue retention. Rarely disclosed; when it is, it is self-reported and definitionally inconsistent between companies.

burn_multiple.description: Net burn / net new ARR. The single best growth-equity efficiency read: under 1.0 is excellent, over 3.0 is buying revenue. Derived, so it inherits the error in both inputs.

next_financing_horizon.description: When the company likely needs to raise again — the moment its terms get repriced.

compute_subsidy_note.description: THE compute-arbitrage question: how much of this company's margin is borrowed from a strategic compute deal rather than earned? A lab with credits from its own investor does not have the gross margin it appears to have.

capital_consumed_per_arr_dollar.description: Derived: total raised / estimated ARR. Net burn is not disclosed for any private company here, so this is the computable stand-in for burn multiple. Under ~3x is efficient; above ~20x the mark is pricing an outcome rather than a business.

capital_efficiency.description: Derived, not reported. Separates capital-intensive toll-collectors from high-margin IP — the distinction gross margin alone cannot make. CoreWeave shows a 65.9% gross margin on capex 3x revenue; Nvidia shows 75.0% on capex under 2% of revenue. Same margin story, opposite businesses.

revenue_per_capex_dollar.description: Annualized revenue / annualized capex. Below ~1.0 means the business is currently buying its revenue with capital.

fcf_conversion_pct.description: FCF / revenue. Where cash actually pools, as opposed to where accounting profit is booked.

asset_intensity.description: Where a company sits on the toll-collector vs IP spectrum. pass_through is the third case: asset-light but thin-margin (integrators, contractors) — Super Micro spends almost nothing on capex at a 10% gross margin and is nobody's idea of high-margin IP.
